presEras.label: The Second Republic
presEras.blurb: Directly elected since 1951, and for thirty-five years a contest between the two governing parties that the SPÖ usually won. The office is powerful on paper, entitled to dismiss the chancellor, and was used carefully.

presEras.label: The Waldheim affair
presEras.blurb: Kurt Waldheim was elected in 1986 after his wartime service in the Wehrmacht surfaced mid-campaign, and spent his term barred from the United States. It was the moment Austria's account of itself as Hitler's first victim stopped being tenable.

presEras.label: The modern presidency
presEras.blurb: Green and independent candidates broke the two-party hold. The 2016 election ran to a runoff, was annulled by the Constitutional Court over the counting of postal votes, and was rerun; Van der Bellen beat the FPÖ's Hofer twice in one year.

legEras.label: The Imperial Council
legEras.blurb: Before there was an Austria there was Cisleithania, the Austrian half of Austria-Hungary, and its House of Deputies is the direct ancestor of the Nationalrat. Its elections were fought in eleven languages. Deputies sat not by party but by club, and the clubs were national before they were ideological: a Poland Club, a Bohemian Club, a Ruthenian Association, an Italian Union. Until 1907 the franchise ran through curiae that weighted a landowner's vote many times a labourer's; the fifth curia added in 1896 gave every man a vote, and only a fraction of the weight. Universal and equal male suffrage arrived in 1907, whereupon the Christian Socials took 96 seats and the Social Democrats 50, and the chamber became so fragmented that it was adjourned more often than it sat. The last of these parliaments was still formally in being when the empire dissolved in 1918.

legEras.label: The First Republic
legEras.blurb: Three camps, socialist, Christian-social and pan-German, each with its own newspapers, sports clubs and paramilitary wing, competing in elections nobody expected to reconcile them. They did not. The Christian Social bloc governed throughout, the Social Democrats held Vienna, and the republic ended in the civil war of 1934 and the Austrofascist state that followed.

legEras.label: Dictatorship and Anschluss
legEras.blurb: No elections. Parliament was dissolved in March 1933 on a procedural pretext, the Social Democrats were crushed in February 1934, and the Anschluss of 1938 delivered Austria to the Reich.

legEras.label: The Proporz republic
legEras.blurb: Two parties, the conservative ÖVP and the socialist SPÖ, took over 90% of the vote between them for four decades and governed together for half of it, dividing the state between them post by post. Turnout ran above 90%. Kreisky's thirteen years gave the SPÖ the only absolute majorities in Austrian history.

legEras.label: The Haider years
legEras.blurb: Jörg Haider took the Freedom Party from 5% to 27% and, in 2000, into government, which brought sanctions from the other fourteen EU members and a coalition that fell apart in Knittelfeld. In the same period the two big parties fell below 60% combined for the first time and the Greens arrived.

legEras.label: Five parties and an Ibiza video
legEras.blurb: Grand coalitions returned without the grandeur: two parties that no longer commanded the country governing it jointly. Then Kurz took the ÖVP right, the FPÖ into coalition, and the whole thing collapsed in 2019 over a secretly filmed evening on Ibiza.

legEras.label: The FPÖ first
legEras.blurb: In September 2024 the Freedom Party came first in a Nationalrat election for the first time, and then could not form a government: coalition talks failed twice before the ÖVP, SPÖ and NEOS assembled a three-party majority to keep it out.

legislative.summary: The first election with the fifth curia, in which every man could vote and almost none of them counted for much. Badeni's language ordinances brought the chamber to a standstill within months and cost him his office.
legislative.caveat: Elected through the curial system, which weighted votes by class and tax: the fifth curia added in 1896 gave every man a vote worth a fraction of a landowner's.

legislative.summary: A parliament of clubs with no majority and no prospect of one, elected over five weeks either side of the new year. Koerber governed largely by emergency decree under Article 14.
legislative.caveat: Elected through the curial system, which weighted votes by class and tax: the fifth curia added in 1896 gave every man a vote worth a fraction of a landowner's.

legislative.summary: The first election under universal and equal male suffrage. The curiae were abolished, the Christian Socials took 96 seats and the Social Democrats 50, and mass politics arrived in the empire all at once.

The last parliament of Austria-Hungary. The German National Association took 100 of 516 seats and nothing resembling a governing majority existed; the chamber was adjourned in 1914 and did not meet again until 1917.
